extraction.Name: Claude Sully
extraction.Refused/Protested: Yes, one time Mr. Covey, who was then Superintendent, came to our house and we were talking about these patents and he asked me if I wanted it and I told him that I did not but he said we would have to take them. This was before the patent had been given to me so when the patent reached me I thought it no use to protest.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: I mortgaged it for $5000.00 all together at two different times.
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Yes, mortgage was finally foreclosed; they took out for taxes, interest commission and abstracts and other things
extraction.NOTES: No one depends on allottee for support except himself; is in good health; received notice of foreclosure and mortgage was finally foreclosed; bought some cattle through the bank that made the mortgage for about $2500.00, received about $300 in cash and a Buick car for $1000.00; patent delivered by mail in 1918; signed receipt for patent; notarized June 7, 1929 before Jas. W. Cross, Notary Public, commission expires 4-28-32
